scope: trait_time and trait_space only; interaction arm is terminal HOLD and its null is not altered

theorem.statement: Under a complete permutation of whole trait states among n labels, the exact permutation expectation of Spearman correlation between a fixed pairwise separation rank vector and pairwise trait-dissimilarity ranks is zero whenever the dissimilarity rank variance is nonzero.
conditions: all unordered label pairs are included in the effect calculation
the null acts by a uniform permutation of the n vertex/state labels
pairwise dissimilarity is a symmetric function of the two assigned states
Spearman ranks use a deterministic tie rule such as average ranks
proof_sketch: A label permutation induces a permutation of the complete graph's unordered edges.
The symmetric group is transitive on unordered edges, so for every fixed edge the expected permuted dissimilarity rank equals the grand mean dissimilarity rank.
Permutation preserves the multiset of dissimilarity ranks, hence its centered norm is constant across permutations.
The fixed separation-rank vector is centered, so its dot product with the expected centered permuted dissimilarity-rank vector is zero.
Therefore the exact mean permutation Spearman correlation is zero.

consequence.canonical_trait_effect: delta_rho = observed Spearman rho exactly, because the exact null mean is zero
consequence.null_permutations_role: retain permutations for null dispersion, diagnostic calibration, and implementation checks; do not inject Monte Carlo error into the null mean
consequence.degenerate_rule: if pairwise dissimilarity has zero rank variance, rho is undefined and the system/replicate fails the predeclared state-variation or informativeness gate

computational_rule.reason: The exact-zero proof and original canonical estimator both apply directly to the complete unordered-pair set.

validation.exact_enumeration_small_n: required in unit tests for continuous and tied categorical synthetic states
validation.permutation_diagnostic: 999 random permutations may be retained to report null SD or verify empirical mean near zero, but are not used to estimate the primary null mean
